Odin × Godot

odin_godot

6 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Script example and SDK featuresQuickstartDocumentationExamplesRepository layoutInstalling (without cloning this repo)Platform statusLicense / attribution

Write Godot scripts in Odin. odin_godot is a Godot 4.7 GDExtension implementing the ScriptLanguageExtension API. Attach a .odin file to a Godot node; generated registration connects its lifecycle procedures, methods, signals, and Inspector properties to the engine. Scripts compile ahead of time to native code and dispatch through a typed registry. The SDK supports custom resources, autoloads, editor tools, multiplayer RPCs, hot reload, and native and WebAssembly exports. A Nix flake pins the development toolchain.

The recorded verification summary covers a 39-test end-to-end suite, including the showcase, example co-op runs, and Asset-Library drop-in layout, through nix develop --command bash tests/run_all.sh. It also includes 7 browser-gated web tests that verify WASM exports in headless Chrome when available. Examples include a pure-Odin coin-collector (tests/showcase/), a complete top-down arena shooter (examples/survivors/), a drop-in co-op cave crawler built with the Kit multiplayer toolkit (examples/cavecrawl/), and a server-authoritative western duel with lag-compensated hitscan on the kit/sim lane (examples/quickdraw/, tested at 240 ms RTT). All of them use zero GDScript gameplay code.

Script example and SDK features#

Odin
//gd:extends Area2D            // base Godot class
//gd:class Coin                // global class_name
package game_scripts

import gd "godot:godot"

Coin :: struct {
	owner:     gd.Area2d,                        // first field stores the engine node handle
	collected: gd.Signal1(int) `gd:"args=value"`, // typed signal field -> collected(value: int)
	value:     gd.Int `gd:"export,range=1:100"`, // @export var with an Inspector slider
	taken:     bool,                             // untagged = private per-instance state
}

coin_ready :: proc(self: ^Coin) {            // lifecycle, matched by name
	if self.value == 0 { self.value = 1 }
}

// Auto-wire body_entered -> this method on _ready (no manual connect call):
@(gd_method, gd_connect = "body_entered")
coin_collect :: proc(self: ^Coin, body: gd.Node2d) {
	if self.taken { return }
	self.taken = true
	coin_emit_collected(self, i64(self.value))   // typed emitter generated from the signal field
	gd.node_queue_free(self.owner)               // gd.* helper queues node deletion
}

In the example, self points to script data and self.owner is the Godot node handle. The generated godot binding exposes the engine API as typed Odin. The gd.* helpers wrap common engine calls and their argument conversions:
Lifecycle _ready / _process / _physics_process / _enter_tree / _exit_tree by proc name
@export every Variant type + Inspector hints (range/enum/multiline/file/resource), groups, defaults, getters/setters, @onready refs
Signals declare (typed gd.Signal0…Signal4 struct fields), emit (typed generated helper), connect (gd.connect_to / @(gd_connect))
Methods @(gd_method): callable from GDScript, as signal targets, and typed cross-script (rt.script_of)
Classes extends any engine class, global class_name, custom resources (.tres), autoload singletons
Editor @tool scripts, gd.is_editor(), custom icons, EditorPlugin, live error squiggles + autocomplete
Multiplayer Kit provides session replication with gd:"replicate" and gd:"owner" fields, commands, generated entity factories, drop-in join, reconnect, and host migration. Its simulation lane adds gd:"predict", fixed ticks, server authority, reconciliation, and bounded lag compensation for contested state. The lanes compose per field (choosing a model); named profiles validate coherent co-op, listen-server, or dedicated settings. @(gd_rpc) remains available for Godot's engine-native path.
Build and export hot reload on save, native desktop export, WebAssembly export
Script modules opt-in script modules: one dll per res://modules/<name>, rebuilt + hot-swapped independently so edits to one module avoid rebuilding unrelated modules
Box3D Authored worlds, shapes, characters and joints, one explicitly stepped backend with distinct Kit/Replay complete-state adapters, and optional editor/debug tools; reference-platform limits are stated in the linked reports

Odin compiles ahead of time, so scripts have no eval/REPL or Godot script-line breakpoints; use lldb for native debugging. Changing @export declarations requires recompilation, which the editor starts on save. See Workflow.

Quickstart#

Shell
nix develop                  # toolchain shell: odin, ols, emcc, llvm/lld, + $GODOT (4.7.1)

# Build the extension + the example's scripts, then play it:
bash build/build_scripts.sh examples/survivors
$GODOT --path examples/survivors          # arrow keys move; auto-fire; survive

# Run the repository's headless suite:
nix develop --command bash tests/run_all.sh
Code
==> phase1  PASS   ==> resources    PASS   ==> editortools  PASS
==> phase2  PASS   ==> crossscript  PASS   ==> debug        PASS
   ...                  ...                    ...
==> survivors PASS ==> web          PASS browser-verified   ALL GREEN

Start with Getting Started to install the toolchain, load the extension in a Godot project, and write a script that moves a node. For multiplayer, the quickstart builds a two-window example in two files. Its simulation version moves motion to server authority. Choose trust and timing settings through network profiles.

Examples#

Play Scrapyard on itch.io to try an Odin + Godot arena shooter in the browser. The repository also includes the Replay Scrapyard port, with a visual guide to its authored scenes, replayable World, input, and presentation.

The Kit overview introduces the multiplayer packages. These three projects demonstrate their use:

  • examples/cavecrawl/ is the co-op reference: a drop-in-join cave crawler exercising every toolkit package (replicated fields, predicted commands + _then consequences, generated entity factory, reconnect, save/resume, host migration, Steam), covered by a latency-injected integration test.
  • examples/slopball/ is the smallest complete kit game: a physics co-op ball pitch (~850 lines), with engine physics replicated through play.Puppet. It shows session setup, entity replication, and gameplay in one project.
  • examples/slopball3d/ uses the same replication model with 3D bodies (play.Puppet3, Node3D containers).

Single-player and engine-plumbing references:

  • examples/survivors/ is a complete top-down arena shooter in pure Odin; each script is commented to teach one slice of the binding (README). Its network layer uses Godot's engine-native path (MultiplayerSpawner/@(gd_rpc)) to demonstrate those APIs. The Kit examples above provide the higher-level session and replication workflow for co-op.
  • examples/coop_arena/ uses one peer-authoritative codebase for engine-native multiplayer over MultiplayerSynchronizer + @(gd_rpc) that runs single-player, over native ENet, and in the browser over WebRTC (room-code lobby) (README). It configures the engine APIs that Kit wraps for session-based games.
  • tests/showcase/ is a minimal pure-Odin coin-collector combining script registration, input, signals, and scene behavior. Run it: $GODOT --path tests/showcase.
  • examples/hello/ is the lowest-level path: a hand-registered GDExtension class (not a script) proving the Odin↔GDExtension ABI.

Repository layout#

dir purpose
flake.nix reproducible toolchain: Odin, ols, LLVM, Emscripten, + $GODOT
bindgen/ generates the typed godot/ package from extension_api.json
godot/ the generated typed binding (Variant, builtins, every class) + the hand-written gd.* Ergonomics_*.odin layer
gdext/, libgd/ the hand-owned GDExtension C-ABI runtime the binding sits on
core/ the extension core (-build-mode:dll): ScriptLanguageExtension, OdinScript, instance dispatch, loader, hot reload, export plugin, editor tooling, web entry
runtime/ the shared registry contract (Class_Desc) imported by both core and scripts
scriptgen/ reads script tags/attributes and generates registration code
build/ the compose+compile pipelines (scripts → dll / wasm; export builds)
tests/ per-feature headless milestones + run_all.sh
docs/ this documentation set

Installing (without cloning this repo)#

The distributable is a drop-in addon: addons/odin_godot/ with prebuilt core dlls, the docs, the build scripts, and a starter template. Get it from the release branch (what the Godot Asset Library entry points at) or build it yourself with nix build .#release, then follow Distribution → Install into a Godot project. The one host tool you need is the odin compiler (the addon README names the tested release and explains the ABI-fingerprint compatibility check).

Platform status#

macOS is the development platform and is verified end-to-end by the suite (including the Asset-Library drop-in layout and the web export). Windows ships prebuilt core dlls and builds scripts natively via build_scripts.ps1, with limited runtime verification so far; Linux is build-verified only. Reports from either platform are very welcome. The crash reporter and build scripts are designed to produce actionable output, so please file what you see.
